name: HB Tórshavn
content:
Havnar Bóltfelag, commonly known as HB Tórshavn, is one of the oldest and most successful football clubs in the Faroe Islands. Founded in 1904 in the capital city of Tórshavn, the club plays its home matches at Gundadalur stadium and competes in the top division of Faroese football. It was originally established by local workers and has remained a central part of the country’s football culture ever since.

The club played an important role in the early development of football in the Faroe Islands, participating in some of the first organized matches and later becoming a founding member of the national league in 1942. After several near successes, HB won its first major titles in 1955, achieving both the league championship and the inaugural national cup. Over time, the team became increasingly dominant, especially in domestic cup competitions, where it set records for consecutive victories and total trophies.

Today, HB Tórshavn is regarded as the most decorated club in Faroese football, with numerous league titles and cup wins to its name. The club has also represented the Faroe Islands in European competitions since the early 1990s, following the country’s admission to UEFA. Despite the challenges of competing internationally, HB remains a leading force domestically and an important symbol of Faroese football tradition.

name: KÍ Klaksvík
content:
Klaksvíkar Ítróttarfelag, commonly known as KÍ Klaksvík, is a Faroese football club based in the town of Klaksvík. Founded in 1904, it is one of the oldest and most successful clubs in the Faroe Islands. The team plays its home matches at Við Djúpumýrar stadium and traditionally wears blue and white colors. Over its history, KÍ has won numerous domestic titles, including more than twenty league championships and several national cups.

The club played a key role in the early development of football in the Faroe Islands and won the very first national league title in 1942. It remained a dominant force for decades, setting records for championships by the end of the 20th century. Although the team experienced setbacks, including relegation in 2009, it quickly returned to the top division and rebuilt its status as a leading club in Faroese football.

In recent years, KÍ Klaksvík has gained international attention through its performances in European competitions. The club made history by becoming the first team from the Faroe Islands to reach the group stage of a major UEFA competition during the 2023–24 UEFA Europa Conference League. This achievement marked a significant milestone not only for the club but also for Faroese football as a whole.

name: B36 Tórshavn
content:
B36 Tórshavn is a Faroese football club based in the capital city of Tórshavn. Founded in 1936, the club competes in the Faroe Islands Premier League and plays its home matches at Gundadalur stadium. It was established by local players who wanted more opportunities to play football, and it quickly became one of the key teams in the country’s football scene.

The club achieved early success by winning its first national championship in 1946 and later securing its first cup title in 1965. Over the decades, B36 developed into one of the most successful clubs in Faroese football, winning multiple league titles and domestic cups. Despite periods of difficulty, it has remained competitive and built a strong reputation for technical and attacking style of play.

In modern times, B36 Tórshavn continues to be a major force in Faroese football, regularly competing at the top level and participating in European competitions. The club is also known for developing local talent and contributing players to the national team. With a long history, strong youth system, and consistent domestic success, B36 remains an important part of football culture in the Faroe Islands.

name: GÍ Gøta
content:
Gøtu Ítróttarfelag, often known simply as GÍ, was a Faroese football club based in the town of Gøta. Founded in 1926, the club played its home matches at Serpugerdi Stadium and was recognized for its yellow and blue colors. It competed for many years in the top division of Faroese football and became one of the notable teams in the country’s domestic scene.

The club enjoyed its greatest success during the 1980s and 1990s, winning six national league titles and six Faroese Cups. A particularly strong period came in the mid-1990s, when GÍ won four consecutive league championships from 1993 to 1996. The team also regularly participated in European competitions, although it was unable to progress beyond the early qualifying rounds.

In 2008, Gøtu Ítróttarfelag merged with Leirvík ÍF to form a new club, Víkingur, marking the end of its independent history. Despite its dissolution, GÍ remains an important part of Faroese football heritage due to its domestic achievements and contribution to the development of the sport in the Faroe Islands.

name: B68 Toftir
content:
B68 Toftir is a Faroese football club based in the village of Toftir on the island of Eysturoy. Founded in 1962, the club competes in the Faroe Islands Premier League and plays its home matches at Svangaskarð stadium, one of the largest venues in the country. It is commonly known simply as B68 and represents a key football institution in its local community.

The club achieved its greatest success during the 1980s and early 1990s, winning three national league titles in 1984, 1985, and 1992. After gaining promotion to the top division in 1980, B68 quickly established itself as a competitive side. Over the years, however, the team has experienced several relegations and promotions, reflecting a fluctuating but resilient presence in Faroese football.

B68 Toftir has also participated in European competitions, including the UEFA Champions League qualifiers and the Intertoto Cup, though it has not advanced beyond early rounds. Domestically, the club has added second-division titles and a national cup-related trophy to its honors. Despite periods outside the top flight, B68 remains an established club with a long history in Faroese football.

name: EB/Streymur
content:
EB/Streymur is a Faroese semi-professional football club based in the villages of Streymnes and Eiði. It was founded in 1993 through a merger between Eiðis Bóltfelag and Streymur, bringing together two smaller clubs into a single team. The club plays its home matches at Við Margáir stadium and competes in the Faroe Islands Premier League.

After its formation, EB/Streymur initially competed in the lower divisions but gradually improved and earned promotion to the top tier around the turn of the century. The team’s rise was supported by the development of local talent and improved facilities. Over time, it established itself as a competitive side in Faroese football, capable of challenging stronger clubs.

The club enjoyed its most successful period in the late 2000s and early 2010s, winning two league titles and four Faroese Cups. EB/Streymur also represented the Faroe Islands in European competitions, gaining experience on the international stage despite limited success. Today, it remains a stable presence in the top division and an important part of Faroese football.

name: NSÍ Runavík
content:
NSÍ Runavík is a Faroese football club based in the town of Runavík on the island of Eysturoy. Founded in 1957, it competes in the Faroe Islands Premier League and plays its home matches at Við Løkin stadium, which has a capacity of around 2,000 spectators. The team is traditionally associated with yellow and black colors and represents one of the key clubs from the eastern part of the islands.

The club achieved its greatest domestic success in 2007, when it won the Faroe Islands Premier League for the first time. In addition to its league title, NSÍ has also won the Faroese Cup three times, in 1986, 2002, and 2017, while reaching several other finals over the years. These achievements established the club as a consistent competitor in domestic football.

NSÍ Runavík has participated in European competitions since 2003, gaining international experience despite limited success in advancing beyond early qualifying rounds. Because its home stadium does not meet UEFA requirements, the team plays European matches at larger venues in other Faroese towns. Today, NSÍ remains a stable presence in the top division and an important part of Faroese football.

name: VB Vágur
content:
VB Vágur, also known as Vágs Bóltfelag, was a Faroese football club based in the town of Vágur on the island of Suðuroy. Founded in 1905, it was one of the early football clubs in the Faroe Islands and played an important role in the development of the sport locally. The team was formed by young enthusiasts who were inspired by football they had seen abroad and began organizing matches in the early years of the club’s existence.

Throughout its history, VB Vágur competed in the top division of Faroese football and achieved notable success, including winning the national league title in 2000 and the Faroese Cup in 1974. The club also reached several cup finals and participated in European competitions such as the UEFA Champions League qualifiers and the Intertoto Cup, although it did not manage to progress beyond the early stages.

In its later years, the club went through several mergers with nearby teams, particularly Sumba, as a response to challenges faced by smaller communities in maintaining strong independent clubs. These mergers eventually led to the creation of VB/Sumba and later FC Suðuroy in 2010, marking the end of VB Vágur as a separate football entity. Despite this, its legacy remains an important part of football history in the Faroe Islands.

name: IF Fuglafjarðar
content:
Ítróttarfelag Fuglafjarðar (commonly known as ÍF) is a Faroese football club based in the town of Fuglafjørður. It was founded in 1946 and has since become the main sports organization of the local community. The club plays its home matches at Í Fløtugerði stadium and traditionally uses red and white colors. It has spent most of its history competing between the top and second tiers of Faroese football.

The club’s greatest achievement came in 1979 when ÍF won its only Faroese top-flight championship. In addition, it has been successful in the second division, winning multiple titles and earning several promotions over the years. Despite this, ÍF has also experienced setbacks, including several lost cup finals, which prevented the club from securing a national cup trophy.

In modern times, ÍF Fuglafjarðar continues to compete in the Faroese league system, often moving between divisions. The club has also participated in European competitions, but without advancing past the early qualifying rounds. Today, it remains an important regional team with a long history and a strong connection to its local community in Fuglafjørður.

name: SÍ Sørvágur
content:
SÍ Sørvágur (Sørvágs Ítróttarfelag) is a Faroese sports club based in the village of Sørvágur on the island of Vágar. It was founded on 17 March 1905 and is one of the older football clubs in the Faroe Islands. The club originally started as a local ball team and later expanded into a broader sports association, also including other sports such as handball and volleyball.

In football, SÍ Sørvágur competed for many decades in the Faroese league system. The club experienced its strongest moment in 1947, when it won the national championship. Over the years, it moved between divisions and faced periods of inactivity or limited success, often influenced by the small population of the village and players leaving for work or fishing.

In the late 1990s and 2000s, SÍ Sørvágur became part of a series of mergers aimed at strengthening football in the region. It first joined FS Vágar and later contributed to the creation of 07 Vestur in 2007. As a result, SÍ Sørvágur ceased to exist as an independent football club, but its legacy remains an important part of local sports history.

name: B71 Sandur
content:
B71 Sandoy is a Faroese football club based in the village of Sandur on the island of Sandoy. It was founded in 1970 and represents several communities across the island under the name Sandoyar Ítróttarfelag B71. The club plays its home matches at the Inni í Dal stadium and is known for its yellow and blue colours. It has become an important sporting institution for the small island community.

The club’s most successful period came in the late 1980s and early 1990s, when it achieved its first and only national league championship in 1989, going through the season unbeaten. During this era, B71 also performed strongly in domestic cup competitions, winning the Faroese Cup in 1993 and reaching additional finals. The team has also spent time in European competitions, although without progressing beyond the early qualifying rounds.

In later years, B71 has moved between divisions in the Faroese football system, often competing in the second tier while occasionally returning to the top flight. Despite its fluctuations in performance, the club remains a stable part of Faroese football and continues to develop local players from Sandoy. It is recognized for its strong community identity and long-standing presence in national competitions.

name: MB Miðvágur
content:
Miðvágs Bóltfelag (commonly known as MB) is a Faroese football club based in the village of Miðvágur on the island of Vágar. It was founded on 21 January 1905 and is one of the oldest football clubs in the Faroe Islands. The club represents its local community and has traditionally been an important part of sports life in the village.

Throughout its history, MB has mostly competed in the lower divisions of Faroese football, with occasional appearances in higher tiers. One of its key moments came after winning promotion and rebuilding following structural changes in Faroese football. The club has experienced several promotions and relegations, reflecting its role as a small but resilient community team.

A major turning point in the club’s history came in 1993, when it merged with SÍF Sandavágur to form FS Vágar. After that project collapsed in 2004, MB was re-established and restarted in the lower divisions. Since then, it has continued to compete in the national league system, maintaining its identity as a historic but modest club from Vágar.

name: Skála ÍF
content:
Skála Ítróttarfelag (commonly known as Skála ÍF) is a Faroese football club based in the village of Skála on the island of Eysturoy. It was founded on 15 May 1965 and represents an important part of the local community’s sporting life. The club plays its home matches at Skála Stadium and is traditionally associated with orange and black colors.

For much of its history, Skála ÍF has moved between the top two divisions of Faroese football. The club experienced one of its strongest periods in the mid-2000s, including a remarkable 2005 season when it finished second in the league and qualified for European competition for the first time. It has also won multiple lower-division titles, showing strong resilience and the ability to rebuild after relegations.

In European competitions, Skála has competed in qualifying rounds of tournaments such as the UEFA Cup and Intertoto Cup, but without advancing beyond the early stages. Despite limited international success, the club remains a stable and respected part of Faroese football, continuing to represent its small community at a national level and developing local players.

name: Víkingur Gøta
content:
Víkingur Gøta is a Faroese football club based in the village of Norðragøta on the island of Eysturoy. It was founded in 2008 as a result of the merger between GÍ Gøta and Leirvík ÍF, combining two established local teams into a single club. The club plays its home matches at Sarpugerði Stadium and quickly became one of the strongest sides in Faroese football.

After its formation, Víkingur established itself in the top division and began competing regularly for domestic titles. The club won its first major trophy in 2009 with the Faroese Cup and went on to become a consistent contender in both league and cup competitions. Its success in the 2010s marked a period of strong growth and stability, including multiple cup victories and European appearances.

Víkingur achieved its greatest league success by winning the Faroese Premier League in 2016, 2017, and again in 2024. The club also made history in European competitions by progressing further than most Faroese teams, reaching advanced qualifying rounds in the UEFA Europa League. Today, it is considered one of the leading clubs in the Faroe Islands with a strong competitive record.

name: TB Tvøroyri
content:
Tvøroyrar Bóltfelag (TB) is a Faroese football club based in the town of Tvøroyri on the island of Suðuroy. It was founded in 1892 and is considered the oldest football club in the Faroe Islands. The club plays its home matches at Við Stórá stadium and is an important part of the local sporting culture in one of the southernmost communities of the country.

TB was one of the founding members of organized Faroese football and took part in the first national competitions when the league system was introduced in 1942. The club experienced its most successful early period in the 1940s to 1980s, winning multiple league titles and several Faroese Cup trophies. Over time, it became known as one of the traditional strong teams in Faroese football history.

In more recent decades, TB has moved between divisions and faced periods of restructuring, including cooperation with other clubs from Suðuroy. Despite these challenges, it continues to compete in the Faroese league system and remains a historic club with deep roots in the development of football in the Faroe Islands.

name: Royn Hvalba
content:
Royn Hvalba (Bóltfelagið Royn) is a Faroese sports club based in the village of Hvalba on the island of Suðuroy. It was founded on 23 October 1923 and is one of the older football clubs in the Faroe Islands. The club represents its local community and has traditionally been an important part of sports life in the village. It plays its home matches at the local stadium in Hvalba.

For much of its history, Royn has competed in the lower tiers of Faroese football, with occasional appearances in higher divisions. One of its most notable achievements was reaching the final of the Faroese Cup in 1983, which remains the club’s strongest cup performance. Over the years, it has also experienced promotions and relegations, reflecting its role as a small but persistent community team.

In recent years, the club has taken part in cooperation projects with other teams from Suðuroy, including temporary mergers at the men’s level. Despite these changes, Royn continues to exist as an independent club, especially in youth and community football. It remains an important part of local identity in Hvalba and continues to develop players for Faroese football.

name: LÍF Leirvík
content:
Leirvíkar Ítróttarfelag (LÍF) was a Faroese football club based in the village of Leirvík on the island of Eysturoy. It was founded on 1 December 1928 and became one of the traditional clubs in Faroese football. The team played its home matches at the Uppi á Brekku stadium and represented a small but active local community.

For most of its history, LÍF competed in the Faroese league system, spending several periods in the top division, particularly during the 1980s and early 1990s. The club’s best league performances came in the mid-1980s when it finished among the stronger teams in the country. It also reached the Faroese Cup final in 1986, where it finished as runner-up, marking its most notable cup achievement.

In 2008, LÍF Leirvík merged with GÍ Gøta to form Víkingur, a new club created to strengthen football in the region. The merger marked the end of LÍF as an independent team, but its history and identity remain part of Faroese football heritage. Many former players and traditions from LÍF continue through the successor club.
